transcripts.onepager_promise: Interprets the full standard text when no vetted value exists, clearly labeled as unvetted
transcripts.prompt: Can I use a Class 5 pole on a 35-degree corner that carries a 75 kVA transformer?
transcripts.assistant_response:
**No — Class 5 isn't enough.** Per unvetted interpretation INT-0318 (DS-315 §3.1, 3.2, 3.6): a 35° angle (>30°) steps up one class, and a 75 kVA transformer (>50 kVA) steps up another — pointing to **Class 3**.

This is a Tier 2 interpretation, not an approved standard. Want me to flag it for an engineer to confirm before you use it in the design?
transcripts.agent_logs:
[EngineeringStandardsAgent] **Tier 2 Interpretation (UNVETTED): INT-0318**

**Question:** Can a Class 5 pole be used on a 35-degree corner structure carrying a 75 kVA transformer?

**Interpretation:** Class 3 is indicated (two class steps above the Class 5 tangent minimum).

| Cited section | What it says |
|---|---|
| DS-315 Pole Selection and Loading, section 3.2, page 9 | Angle structures above 30 degrees step up one pole class. |
| DS-315 Pole Selection and Loading, section 3.6, page 12 | A pole-mounted transformer above 50 kVA adds one further class step. |
| DS-315 Pole Selection and Loading, section 3.1, page 8 | The straight-line minimum is Class 5 (vetted row QR-315-01). |

**Why unvetted:** The answer combines two sections; no vetted row covers angle plus transformer loading.

Not authoritative. Confirm with a standards engineer before using it in a design.

**Risk: High (score 9)** — driven by work near energized lines, a span over a public road, steep access at two sites, and a planned outage.

- DS-210 — Overhead Line Clearances
